subject: POC lab alignment — routing tiers & failover practice
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acme-fin.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC lab alignment — routing tiers & failover practice

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the time on the call last week. We'd like to kick off a hands-on POC session to run through three things: prompt validation (sample prompts you sent), routing policy walkthrough (model selection, tiering, region routing, fallback rules), and a short load test to validate throughput and KV cache behavior.

Proposed slots (US/PST):
- Tue 15 Jun, 10:00–12:00 (deep-dive + short load test)
- Wed 16 Jun, 08:00–10:00 (morning slot for your devs)

Please let me know which works best and who from your side will attend (SRE, product, legal for any brief compliance Qs). I've attached a short POC checklist and sample prompts to prep.

Agenda (high level):
1) 15 min intro + goals
2) Prompt review and safety checks (30 min)
3) Routing policy design: tiers, regions, fallbacks (40 min)
4) Load test run and metrics review (25 min)
5) Next steps & action items (10 min)

If neither slot works, send a couple alternatives and we'll adapt.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Attachment: POC-checklist.pdf; sample-prompts.csv

From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acme-fin.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme-fin.com>, Jared Miller <jared@cloudops.co>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 12:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC lab alignment — routing tiers & failover practice

Thanks Stephanie — really appreciate the detailed agenda. Quick note on availability: Tue 15 Jun in the late morning runs into our weekly exec sync (we can't shift that this month). Wed 16 Jun 08:00–10:00 PT looks better for our engineers, but Jared (cloudops) is only available after 09:00.

Can we start at 09:15 PT on Wed and run to 11:15? That gives Jared time to join for the load testing portion. Attendees from our side: me (product), Samantha (SRE), Jared (cloudops).

Also, curious whether you can run the load test in our staging region (us-east-1) rather than a Redwood default — we want to exercise cross-region routing and the fallback paths. If that's possible, call that out and we'll make short-lived credentials available.

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Gomez
Director, Product — Acme Financial
alex.gomez@acme-fin.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acme-fin.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC lab alignment — routing tiers & failover practice

Alex — perfect, thanks for the preference and attendee list. 09:15–11:15 PT on Wed 16 Jun works for our team. I'll send a calendar invite once I confirm a couple internal logistics.

Quick technical notes so Marissa (runtime lead) and Connor (solutions) can prep:
- We'll schedule load testing from your staging (us-east-1) and exercise region-based routing + a simulated failure for fallback to our secondary region. Marissa: can your team stand up a small test target there?
- Prompt set: we'll use sample-prompts.csv but would like one or two high-priority prompts you want to validate first — can Samantha drop those into the Drive folder?
- Please confirm whether there are any internal firewall rules we should be aware of for the test VM.

Attachments: routing-tier-matrix.xlsx (draft) — this maps model tiers we typically propose (high-accuracy vs low-latency) and candidate fallback models. We can update during the session.

Also, conditional note on timing: our PM who owns quant/quantization profiles is OOO in the morning but Connor can cover model/quant recommendations.

Thanks — will follow up with the invite and pre-reads.

Best,
Stephanie

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@acme-fin.com>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme-fin.com>, Jared Miller <jared@cloudops.co>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC lab alignment — routing tiers & failover practice

Steph,

Couple of quick operational items from runtime:
- We can run the load test in us-east-1 and trigger the fallback to us-west-2 by toggling our routing policy (we'll simulate a degraded AZ via throttling). I'll bring a script to perform the failover test and capture latency/p99s.
- For the load test, recommend limiting to ~50 concurrent connections for the first run so we can validate caching behavior without blowing quotas. If Acme wants to scale up after first run, we'll do a second burst.
- I'll add a short slide to the Drive folder showing the metric dashboard we'll use (link in Drive).

Jira note for follow-up action: SUP-1102 (set up temporary test IAM role and short-lived credentials for Acme staging). Connor, can you create that role and share the ARN before EOD Tue?

On agenda tweaks: suggest we swap the prompt validation and routing policy blocks (do routing first). Reason: routing decisions will determine which model variants we exercise during prompt tests, and it will make the load test more representative.

-M

--
Marissa Cole
Runtime Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
